title: The 2026 World Cup Format Explained: 48 Teams, 12 Groups, 104 Matches
speaker: Extra Time Explained
description: A clear, evergreen explainer of how the expanded 2026 FIFA World Cup works — 48 teams, 12 groups, the new round of 32, and 104 matches across the USA, Canada, and Mexico.
summary: This video explains the brand-new format of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the first hosted by three nations — the United States, Canada, and Mexico — across 16 host cities. For the first time the tournament expands from 32 teams to 48, split into 12 groups of four (Group A through Group L). Each team plays three group matches, earning three points for a win, one for a draw, and zero for a loss. The top two teams in every group qualify (24 teams), and the eight best third-placed teams also advance, creating a brand-new round of 32. The narrator walks through why finishing third is no longer automatic elimination, how goal difference becomes a 'tournament within a tournament', and why the expansion to 104 matches makes the World Cup bigger, longer, and harder to predict. Clear, measured narration suitable for intermediate English learners. (Placeholder summary — enriched by prefetch Phase B.)
